sample_unit: patients (held-out test set from 250 patients in the Discharge-Me benchmark)

links.outcome: Sentence-level detection of faithfulness hallucinations in LLM-generated discharge summaries (F1, recall, precision)
links.effect: Fine-tuned Qwen3-14B detector: E4 F1 0.831 (90.9% recall, 76.5% precision); E3+E4 F1 0.823, a 50.0% relative improvement over base model and better than RAGTruth-style and QAGS-style baselines.
links.quote: Our fine-tuned Qwen3-14B detection model achieves an F1 of 0.831 on the safety-critical E4 metric (90.9% recall, 76.5% precision) and an F1 of 0.823 on E3+E4, representing a 50.0% relative improvement over the base model and outperforming RAGTruth-style and QAGS-style baselines.

unlisted_practices: GraphRAG patient-level knowledge graph verification of generated clinical text
Four-grade sentence-level evidence classification (E1-E4) producing evidence chains
Closed-loop generation-detection pipeline for discharge summaries
Reusing detector annotations as datasets for downstream training and distillation

screen.reason: Evaluates a multi-agent GraphRAG-based hallucination detection and verification framework (guardrail) for checking clinical discharge summaries against source EHR data.
